stories.primary_headline: CBSE announces date sheet for class 10 and 12 board examinations 2027

primary_source.headline: CBSE announces date sheet for class 10 and 12 board examinations 2027
primary_source.content: New Delhi: After a delay, the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) finally announced the dates for class 10 and 12 examinations. Exams for both the classes will begin on February 16, with physics being the first paper for Class 12 and painting the first for Class 10. The exams will conclude on March 9 for Class 10 and April 9 for Class 12.The exams, which will be held offline in pen-paper model, will be conducted across 86 subjects for Class 10, and for Class 12, students will appear across 121 subjects.CBSE Board Exams 2027: Practical exams from January 1; Class 10, 12 date sheet awaited“Adequate gaps have been provided between examinations of subjects commonly offered together by students in both Class X and Class XII. The tentative schedules of major entrance examinations for Class XII students have been taken  into account. Every effort has been made to complete the Board Examinations well before the commencement of such entrance examinations, enabling students to manage their preparation effectively,” CBSE said in a release. The board also said that it has further taken into account the number of candidates appearing on a particular day at each examination centre to facilitate smooth conduct of examinations. They added that the schedule was designed to minimise the prolonged absence of teachers from their schools during the evaluation process.In all, the Board said, it factored in 40,000 subject combinations while designing the exam sheet.

stories.primary_headline: "Not applied its mind..." Gauhati High Court quashes Pranab Doley's detention order under NSA

primary_source.headline: "Not applied its mind..." Gauhati High Court quashes Pranab Doley's detention order under NSA
primary_source.content: Guwahati: More than 100 days after Pranab Doley, an indigenous rights activist in Assam, was detained under the National Security Act (NSA), Gauhati High Court on Friday quashed the order of his detention on the ground that the same was legally unsustainable.While quashing the detention order, the court observed that the detaining authority did not apply its mind as to whether or not the ordinary laws of the country was insufficient to deal with the activities of the petitioner.The bench of justice Kalyan Rai Surana and Justice Susmita Phukan Khaund had reserved its judgment on October 14. The 34-page judgment was pronounced on Friday.'He just raised voice for people, did nothing anti-national': Father of NSA detenue Pranab Doley Doley, who allegedly led indigenous farmers near Kaziranga National Park for a protest against construction of a five-star hotel allegeldly without properly compensating them, was arrested on July 13. He was, however, granted bail on July 29 but was detained under the NSA a day later. In the detention order, the state home department claimed that Doley was booked in several criminal cases in the past and his prevention detention was necessary in view of possibility of him continue to indulge in "activities prejudicial to maintenance of law and order." The court set aside the detention order on the grounds that Doley, 40, was detained on the strength of "stale cases," including those in which he had been discharged and acquitted. The court said out of the 13 cases, Doley had been acquitted in nine while legal process was underway in the rest. The bench said although the detaining authority alleged Doley's involvement in road blockades and damages to public properties, no particulars of the alleged offence, including place, dateand time of commission of such alleged offences have been disclosed. "Thus, the allegations against the petitioner is vague and bereft of material particulars..."The court said relevant facts and grounds of his detention and relevant documents were not furnished to Doley, disallowing him to make an effective representation before the prescribed authorities. The authorities also did not act on his representation against his detention, the court said. Foreign trips: The HC said although the home department claimed that Doley had visited foreign countries 14 times, it did not give the details of anti-India activity by the petitioner. "The grounds of detention also does not specify in which foreign visit the petitioner made any speech or statement which has brought disrepute to the country or has encouraged seditious activity against the country. There is no information as to where the petitioner gave any speech or statement, which had the potential to threaten the security or integrity of the country, territorial, moral, political, social, or otherwise."The bench said Doley's repetitive foreign visits, by itself, is not an act which would warrant preventive detention of a person and curtail his fundamental right to visit a country of his choice. "....except for a vagu allegation regarding foreign visits and suspicious foreign exchange receipts, the detaining authority has not furnished to the petitioner any materials showing how his foreign visits and receipt of foreign exchange amounts to activities that is prejudicial to the interest of the State, its security and integrity, or has affected public order," the court said.Three lawyers, Santanu Borthakur, Dipesh Kumar Agarwala and S. Dey appeared on behalf of Doley. Timeline of eventsDoley, who did Master in Social Work from TISS, Mumbai, was arrested on July 13 following a protest against construciton of a 5-star hotel near Kaziranga National Park without allegedly compensating the indigenous farmers.He was granted bail on July 29.He was detained under the NSA on July 30.State home department claimed that Doley's prevention detention was necessary in view of possibility of him continue to indulge in "activities prejudicial to maintenance of law and order." His father Lakhi Doley had said Pranab was detained for raising voice for the indigenous farmers.

stories.primary_headline: Crackerless Diwali must be people’s movement, not a court order: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Crackerless Diwali must be people’s movement, not a court order: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said a crackerless Diwali should be a people’s movement, not a judicial initiative, as it slammed the commercialisation of festivals and observed that restrictions alone cannot curb Delhi’s pollution crisis. “No restriction is going to work. The more orders we pass, the more violations will multiply,” a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant remarked while hearing the suo motu case on air pollution in Delhi-NCR.Anti-pollution measures doomed unless authorities enforce directions on ground: Supreme Court  “We keep talking, make statements but point is AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI remarked, while urging the Centre and states to educate farmers on the economics of stubble burning. The court said only a people’s movement for a crackerless Diwali and responsible celebration can save Delhi.&nbsp; The city-wide Air Quality Index stood around 389 to 391 in the ‘very poor’ category, with several areas slipping towards ‘severe’, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, also on the bench, said commercialisation of festivals was a major problem.&nbsp; The CJI agreed, noting that the rich had turned Diwali gift exchange into a social and status symbol, fuelling waste and pollution. “Why don’t we revert to our original customs,” the CJI asked, stressing that celebrations must be accompanied by responsibility towards the environment. Diwali was meant to be a festival of lights, not a festival of smoke, he said. The court flagged bumper-to-bumper traffic in Delhi-NCR and questioned authorities on anti-pollution measures. It made clear that the poor should not be blamed for the crisis.&nbsp; “Poor people do not generate any pollution. They are the sufferers. It is those who can afford it and those who can contribute to it,” the CJI remarked.&nbsp; He also noted that Diwali is an important livelihood period for those dependent on seasonal work and that this aspect should be considered. The Centre’s counsel attributed the rise in pollution to the festive season and movement of people.&nbsp;Protests can't choke livelihoods: Supreme Court on demonstrations in Delhi's Ramlila Maidan ahead of festive period  The bench said it would go by expert opinion on closing physical classes in schools if the AQI rises further. It urged governments to educate farmers, observing that they would stop burning stubble once they understood the economics. A crackerless Diwali cannot be imposed and must be embraced by the people, the court said.

primary_source.content: Andy Burnham says it isn't fair if an employer 'holds all the cards' The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible". It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination. However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable. Burnham said the current system felt "weighted against the applicant" and the changes were aimed at "tilting the scales back". "It can be quite soul destroying for young people these days, applying for jobs when the salary is not listed but sometimes they're not getting a reply," he told the BBC. The prime minister added that publishing salaries in adverts was also important for closing the gender pay gap.

primary_source.content:
Ubuntu has CVE-2026-98432 marked as a 9.8, but yet it's coming up on a week with no update to fix it.  It's still marked as "work in progress" (though at least now they've listed a mitigation):https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-98432I've had mitigations in place for a week, but this response is really shaking my confidence in Ubuntu. primary_source.content: New Delhi: Social media platforms must assume greater responsibility for the content they host, take necessary steps to ensure child safety, ensure algorithmic transparency, and provide citizens with an effective mechanism to address grievances, Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Friday.Speaking on the evolving nature of the internet and social media landscape, Vaishnaw asserted that platforms can no longer remain passive. They must proactively protect society from serious online harms, including “digital arrest” scams, he said. Kolkata teen blindfolded, set ablaze; police arrest 3, assault allegedly filmed for social media reel “Today, social media platforms must take the responsibility for child safety, for women’s safety, for digital arrest, for the harms which come to the citizens… social media platforms must take proactive steps. Unlike the past, they must take proactive steps to make sure that our society is safe,” said Vaishnaw, who also holds the Information and Broadcasting portfolio.The minister stressed the need to give ordinary citizens a stronger voice on these platforms. Currently, he noted, when content causes serious harm, the only options available are approaching the courts or the police. He called for a robust and effective grievance redressal system that allows people to seek remedies directly.“If something is there on the social media platforms which causes serious harm to the citizens, the citizens have only the recourse to go to the courts or go to the police. There has to be a good, very effective mechanism by which the citizens get voice to address their grievances,” Vaishnaw said.

stories.primary_headline: Tempted by snacks before bed? Here's why - and what you can do about it

primary_source.headline: Tempted by snacks before bed? Here's why - and what you can do about it
primary_source.content: So, why are evening cravings so common? And what can you do to keep them in check? Love a bedtime snack? You're not alone Despite the fact we spend longer going without food when we are sleeping, research suggests our appetite naturally peaks in the evening, almost regardless of how much we have eaten earlier in the day. Prof James Betts, who researches how the body handles food and energy at the University of Bath, says a big factor is that our "hunger hormone" ghrelin is generally higher later in the day. "While it tends to be suppressed by meals, that really only happens after the first meal of the day, not after lunch or dinner." But what you eat also matters. Meals rich in protein, fibre and volume tend to keep us satisfied for longer.

stories.primary_headline: Exclude vacancies in KK from KPSC purview: Priyank Kharge

primary_source.headline: Exclude vacancies in KK from KPSC purview: Priyank Kharge
primary_source.content: Kalaburagi: District In-charge Minister Priyank Kharge has directed officials to exclude current vacant posts in the Kalyana Karnataka region from the purview of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) and instead fill them on a priority basis through the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA).He issued the direction while participating in a meeting of the sub-committee on the development of the Kalyana Karnataka region and the implementation of Article 371(J) of the Constitution held at Vikasa Soudha on Friday.Stating that Article 371(J) of the Constitution was introduced with the objective of ensuring comprehensive development of the Kalyana Karnataka region and providing fair opportunities in education and employment to its people, Kharge said that the officials must treat this significant constitutional mandate with the utmost seriousness. He warned that any form of negligence or delay in the implementation of this provision will not be tolerated.Article 371(J) is a significant constitutional measure, implemented through considerable effort, aimed at the development and protection of the rights of the people of the Kalyana Karnataka region. However, the officials are failing to demonstrate the expected level of seriousness in providing the benefits envisioned by this provision.The people of Kalyana Karnataka rightfully demanding the benefits—such as access to education and employment—to which they are entitled under this provision.Karnataka HC reconstitutes SIT to probe KPSC scam; Hitendra is new chiefThis is a right granted to them by the Constitution itself. Therefore, officials must not treat the implementation of Article 371(J) light, he explained.“The minister said that lack of progress in implementing the clear directives issued during the last meeting indicates that officials have not taken those instructions seriously. Directives issued during meetings should not be confined merely to official records. These must be implemented within a stipulated timeframe, and clear statistics regarding the progress achieved should be presented at the next meeting. The departments must work in co-ordination on matters concerning the development of the Kalyana Karnataka region,” he said.The minister urged officials from the concerned departments to take immediate action to accelerate the process of filling vacant posts in the Kalyana Karnataka region, and to ensure that the constitutional benefits guaranteed to the people of this region under Article 371(J) are effectively delivered.

stories.primary_headline: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest

primary_source.headline: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
primary_source.content: Evidence of digging and new buildings are visible in satellite imagery taken in November at the Garmdareh military base in Karaj near the capital Tehran and the Shahroud base in the north, analysts at British intelligence company MAIAR, who reviewed the photos, told BBC Verify. At least 12 other military sites, including missile complexes and air bases, appear to show signs of repairs. New roofs have been built on destroyed buildings at the Kermanshah missile base in western Iran, near the border with Iraq, while damaged buildings and debris have been cleared at the Parchin military complex - which has been repeatedly repaired despite a succession of air strikes - east of the capital. The excavations near Shahroud could potentially be related to the production of missiles, said Jim Lamson, a former CIA analyst who focused on Iran. He said that because the nearby air base at Shahroud has been targeted multiple times in recent years, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) is probably trying to find ways to move its production facilities underground. A MAIAR analyst said that Iran has "a pattern of moving infrastructure underground to protect them from further strikes". Mark Mellett, a defence analyst and former head of the Irish military, said the construction of underground facilities had the added benefit of making it "harder for outside observers to assess the extent and operational status". At multiple bases across the country, Iranian forces have focused on carrying-out small-scale repairs to complexes which have been heavily damaged by air strikes since the start of the US-Israeli war. Analysts said that satellite images appear to show that significant construction has been completed at the Taleghan 2 facility at the Parchin military complex, with damaged buildings levelled and the aftermath of attacks on an underground bunker repaired and reinforced with concrete.

stories.primary_headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths

primary_source.headline: Minister raises concern over rising number of maternal deaths
primary_source.content: Chitradurga: The rising number of maternal deaths despite the availability of modern facilities in hospitals is a matter of concern as maternal and infant mortality can be reduced if medical officers closely monitor the health of pregnant women, Health and Minority Welfare Minister U T Khader said.He was speaking at a progress review meeting of the health and minority welfare departments held at the deputy commissioner's office auditorium on Friday.Kannada vocabulary, dialects, folk knowledge and literary heritage must be preserved: Minister UT KhaderEven if pregnant women show minor signs of complications, they should immediately be shifted to the district hospital by ambulance. They should be admitted to hospitals at least three days before delivery. Doctors should ensure the health of both mother and child during childbirth. If serious complications arise, they should be referred to the district hospital. Awareness programmes must also be conducted in rural areas, he said.Four maternal deaths have been reported in the current year. The women died due to high blood pressure and lung infections. Compared to last year, the maternal mortality rate in the district has declined by 50%, District Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) Officer D M Abhinav said.Khata campaign sees 11,000 visitors in four weeks'Visit PHCs'The minister directed taluk health officers to visit and inspect primary health centres under their jurisdiction at least three times a month.During every visit, officers should identify deficiencies and problems and take steps to address them and introduce necessary improvements, he said.Meetings involving local MLAs, organisations and hospital staff should be held at least once a month. Hospitals should not have to wait for government funds for renovation, cleaning of toilets or painting. It is the responsibility of taluk health officers to seek assistance from local MLAs and organisations to renovate and maintain hospitals, he said.Minority schoolsResidential schools and colleges under the Minority Welfare Department should give importance to sports and extracurricular activities alongside quality education. It was encouraging that SSLC results in the district's APJ Abdul Kalam, Morarji Desai and Maulana Azad residential schools had exceeded 90%, he said.MLA K C Veerendra, Urban Development Authority chairperson M K Tajpeer, Deputy Commissioner S Ramya, Assistant Commissioner K Kantaraj, Health Department district nodal officer Ranganath, District Health Officer M C Sunil Kumar, District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority chairperson R Shivanna, and vice-chairperson D N Mailarappa, were present.Process e-khata applications in two days, open 10 PSK-style centres in Bengaluru: D K ShivakumarOutside prescriptionsIn another progress review meeting held at the Hiriyur City Municipal Council hall on Friday, Health Minister U T Khader warned government hospital doctors of strict action if they prescribe medicines that patients are required to purchase from outside."The government is supplying all necessary medicines to patients. Asking them to buy medicines from outside amounts to exploiting the poor. This should not continue," he warned.

stories.primary_headline: Looming water crisis: Lad asks officials to take preventive steps

primary_source.headline: Looming water crisis: Lad asks officials to take preventive steps
primary_source.content: Dharwad: District In-charge Minister Santosh Lad has urged people to use water judiciously and avoid wastage, warning that the severity of drought in the coming days cannot be predicted.Speaking at the KDP progress review meeting held at the Zilla Panchayat auditorium here on Friday, Lad said the possibility of a major water crisis in the coming days could not be ruled out and stressed the need for advance preparations by the government and public cooperation.He said discussions had already been held with officials of various departments on precautionary measures. The administration had identified vulnerable areas and taken decisions to tackle possible water shortages. Officials were directed to effectively implement schemes aimed at addressing drinking water problems.Lad warned that criminal cases would be registered against officials found negligent in implementing or maintaining water supply projects. Senior officers should monitor the performance of their subordinates daily and assign specific responsibilities to each official. Those failing to discharge their duties would face suspension, he said.MLA Abbayya Prasad expressed concern over the growing garbage menace in the twin cities. He urged the municipal corporation to prioritise waste management and ensure regular garbage clearance.He said civic officials should not restrict themselves to office work but conduct field inspections. Despite the appointment of zonal officers and provision of vehicles, the expected results had not been achieved. He suggested installing CCTV cameras at garbage dumping points and imposing fines on those violating waste disposal rules. Senior officials should also monitor the functioning of health inspectors and take action against those neglecting their duties.MLA N H Konaraddi stressed the need for officials to bring public and departmental issues to the notice of the concerned authorities without delay or concealing problems. Regular field visits and inspections were essential to understand and resolve public grievances, he said.Drought deepens drinking water crisis in Haveri districtMLA Vinay Kulkarni asked officials to respond responsibly to farmers’ and public grievances. Expressing concern over alleged corruption in government offices, he warned officials to curb the practice. Citing fodder shortage in the district, he directed that fodder should not be sold outside the district or state and that fodder supplied by the district administration should meet quality standards.He also directed the Superintendent of Police to investigate allegations that certain RTI activists were extorting money from government officials in the district.MLC F H Jakkappanavar called upon officials to ensure that SC and ST communities received their rightful reservation benefits and government grants. stories.primary_headline: IISc honours eight alumni for contributions to science, technology and society

primary_source.headline: IISc honours eight alumni for contributions to science, technology and society
primary_source.content: Bengaluru:&nbsp;This year, the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) honours eight scientists and engineers with its Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna Awards and Young Alumnus/Alumna Medals.The awards recognise alumni/ae who have made exceptional contributions to their professions, to society, and to the Institute. Each nomination is assessed by a committee under the oversight of the Director, IISc.This year's Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna awardees are B S Manjunath, Dipakar Das Sarma, Jagannath Nayak, Maruthi R Akella, and Rajat Moona. The Young Alumnus/Alumna Medals, given to researchers under the age of 40, are conferred on Abhishek Sinha, Geethu Joseph, and Himanshu Joshi.The awardees will be honoured at a ceremony to be held on 19 December 2026, at the JN Tata Auditorium, IISc.Distinguished Alumnus/Alumna Awardees1. B S Manjunath is a globally recognised computer scientist and academic leader, and the Frank Koenig Distinguished Chair in Signals and Systems and Distinguished Professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, USA. His work spans computer vision, content-based image retrieval, and biological image informatics, including BisQue, an open-source platform for scientific image management adopted as a core service of NSF CyVerse. He contributed foundational video descriptors to the MPEG-7 standard, co-founded the company Mayachitra, and has supervised 53 PhD graduates.B S Manjunath i 2. Dipankar Das Sarma is an internationally renowned condensed matter physicist and materials chemist, currently the ANRF National Science Chair and Emeritus Professor at the Solid State and Structural Chemistry Unit, IISc. His work includes the discovery of the covalent-insulator state, kinetic energy-driven ferromagnetism in Sr2FeMoO6, and depth-sensitive photoemission techniques for probing nanocrystals and buried interfaces. He also spearheaded India's access to international synchrotron facilities, establishing Indo-Italian beamlines at Elettra.&nbsp;Dipankar Das SarmaCentralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru 3. Jagannath Nayak is a distinguished defence scientist and Director General of Missiles and Strategic Systems at DRDO. His career spans photonics, fibre lasers, and inertial navigation. He led the indigenous development of high-accuracy Fibre Optic Gyroscopes for programmes such as Akash, Nag, and Astra, and the creation of India's first operational Laser Directed Energy Weapon system. His work has led to complete indigenisation of critical avionics and laser systems.&nbsp;Jagannath Nayak 3. Maruthi R Akella is a globally renowned aerospace scientist and control systems engineer, who currently holds the Cockrell Family Chair in Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin, USA. His research covers spacecraft attitude estimation, adaptive control, vision-guided robotics, and orbital mechanics. His algorithms provided onboard guidance for Intuitive Machines' IM-1 lunar lander mission, the first US moon landing in over 50 years.&nbsp;Maruthi R Akella 4. Rajat Moona is an internationally renowned computer scientist and technologist, and Director of IIT Gandhinagar. His work has shaped India's digital infrastructure, from the Smart Card OS Template Architecture (SCOSTA) behind driving licences and e-passports to India's Electronic Toll Collection system and FASTag. He architected the M3 Electronic Voting Machine, VVPAT, and the National Voters' Service Portal, and as Director General of C-DAC, advanced national supercomputing through PARAM Yuva II.&nbsp;Rajat Moona Young Alumnus/Alumna Medallists1. Abhishek Sinha is a leading theoretical computer scientist, currently a Reader at the School of Technology and Computer Science, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai. He has resolved long-standing open problems in online learning and network optimisation, including a framework that achieves optimal learning and long-term constraint satisfaction simultaneously. His work has appeared in venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, and IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking.&nbsp;Abhishek Sinha 2. Geethu Joseph is a tenured Assistant Professor at Delft University of Technology, Netherlands. Her work introduces frameworks for resource-aware control systems and sensing methods for autonomous driving, radar, and wireless communications, with industrial partners including NXP, ASML, imec, and TNO. She is an Associate Editor of the IEEE Sensors Journal.&nbsp;Geethu Joseph 3. Himanshu Joshi a researcher in computational biophysics, multiscale molecular simulations, DNA nanotechnology, and an Assistant Professor of Biotechnology at IIT Hyderabad. His work spans aquaporins, ion channels, nanopore sequencing, and water desalination, including artificial water channels for ultrafast water transport and DNA origami-based ion channels.Himanshu Joshi

stories.primary_headline: Steps being taken to curb man-animal conflict in Bandipur: Minister Ramalinga Reddy

primary_source.headline: Steps being taken to curb man-animal conflict in Bandipur: Minister Ramalinga Reddy
primary_source.content: Gundlupet: Minister of Forest, Ecology and Environment Ramalinga Reddy assured that necessary measures are being taken to prevent man-animal conflict in Bandipur forest area.Speaking to media persons, here on Friday, he said, "There is no delay in the probe related to the shootout incident by the Forest department in Hanur, which claimed three lives. The CoD is investigating and we will not intervene. The anti-poaching camps and quarters that were destroyed by mob after the incident are being repaired. The department personnel need not fear and should perform their duties. Besides, there is no permission to possess rifles without licenses. Those possessing the same should surrender to the government, or face legal action."Necessary steps would be taken for the establishing Kaniyanapura elephant corridor of Bandipur Tiger Reserve. Private land if any, would be acquired for the project, he said.Tribal woman killed in tiger attack near Bandipur Reserve in MysuruDiscussions have been held with the State Wildlife Board on announcing M M Hills as Tiger reserve, but locals are against it. The government will take a final decision soon, he said. On illegal resorts and homestays at eco-sensitive zones at Bandipur, he said, permission is given only to resorts that have licenses. Notices are served to those operating without licenses. Some have stay orders from the court. The supervisory committee will monitor this. Reddy held a meeting with the Forest Department officials on the human-animal conflict in the region and gathered information.Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (PCCF) Kumar Pushkar said, "34 people have died due to wild animal attacks in Chamarajanagar district in the last 11 months, and tops the district. Kodagu is in second place. Thirty one tigers have been safely rescued in the last one year."The railway barricades have been useful and the government should grant funds for erecting barricades for 73-kms, he appealed to the minister.Bandipur Conservator of Forest Nandish said, "There are 13 ranges in Bandipur, covering around 1,036 kms. In all, 136 villages come under the forest area. Totally 314 personnel are on duty, with 213 watchers on outsourced basis."Artificial Intelligence cameras and drones are being used to monitor the movement of the wild animals. With this, we get information on the movement of elephants and wild animals near the villages and help to alert the villagers, he said.Reddy said that out of 13 ranges in Bandipur, only four ranges have no man-animal conflict. "Around 38% of the forest is covered with lantana. The biodiversity will be affected if machines are used for clearing it and the forest will be affected if left unattended. Hence, measures would be taken to clear them without affecting the forest," he said.MLA M Ganesh Prasad, APCCF Manoj Ranjan, CCF Malathi Priaya, Ravishankar CF, Mysuru Circle, ACF Paramesh, Vinod were present.

stories.primary_headline: Spate of bomb threats poses serious challenge to airline industry

primary_source.headline: Spate of bomb threats poses serious challenge to airline industry
primary_source.content: More fake bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe Some of the threats apparently came from phone calls, others via email, and although they have all turned out to be hoaxes, they were each clearly serious enough to force emergency action. Some planes had to be escorted by military jets, others were quietly inspected mid-air by cabin crew - desperate not to cause alarm. A number had to be re-routed from their original destinations, landing at different airports, sometimes in different countries. An Aer Lingus flight had to land at an airbase 1,000 kilometers from its intended destination after running low on fuel. All this poses a serious challenge to the airlines, who have little idea who is causing the severe disruption they have faced almost every day this week. Although so far all threats have turned out to be hoaxes, airlines have no choice but take each threat seriously.

stories.primary_headline: Amit Shah sounds poll bugle in Uttarakhand; promises UCC in all BJP governed states

primary_source.headline: Amit Shah sounds poll bugle in Uttarakhand; promises UCC in all BJP governed states
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Sounding the poll bugle in Uttarakhand, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday said that the BJP will slowly implement Uniform Civil Code in all states governed by the saffron party. He called for the party leaders to ensure that the party wins 65 seats in the upcoming Assembly elections.Addressing a rally in Dehradun on the occasion of Uttarakhand’s State Foundation Day, Shah said that after the implementation of the UCC in Uttarakhand, 15 other states had moved forward in the direction of introducing the legislation.“Our government will implement the UCC in all the states governed by our party,” he said.Congress top leaders review preparations in poll-bound states of Manipur and UttarakhandUttarakhand became the first state in the country to implement the UCC in January 2025. The legislation provides a common framework for personal laws governing matters such as marriage, divorce and inheritance.Shah also asked party leaders and workers to intensify their outreach ahead of the elections scheduled early next year, seeking a third consecutive term for the BJP in the state.“Last time, you gave us 47 seats. But this time, we have to move forward with the target of 65-plus seats,” Shah said, referring to the BJP’s performance in the 2022 Assembly elections.The BJP had won 57 seats in the 2017 Assembly elections and 47 in 2022 in the 70-member Uttarakhand Assembly.Shah said the BJP wanted to make Uttarakhand a “secure and prosperous” state and transform Devbhoomi into the country’s “cultural capital”.The home minister also targeted the Congress, accusing it of leaving Uttarakhand dependent on a “money-order economy” and migration, while claiming that the BJP had worked to establish an industrial economy in the state.He highlighted infrastructure projects, including the Delhi-Dehradun economic corridor and the Rishikesh-Karnaprayag railway line, and said the government had undertaken efforts to curb migration from border villages.The home minister also attacked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his “Vote Bachao Yatra”, alleging that it was actually a “Ghuspaithiya Bachao Yatra”.Shah said BJP workers would reach out to people across the state and seek their support for the party’s third consecutive term.

stories.primary_headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director

primary_source.headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director
primary_source.content: Mangaluru:&nbsp;Technology and digital advancements must be guided by character, commitment and compassion to ensure their meaningful use for the welfare of society, said Prof Vivek Lal, Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh.Addressing 16th convocation of Nitte Deemed to be University at Deraakatte, he urged students to draw inspiration from Swami Vivekananda's ideals and uphold the values of character, commitment and compassion, which he described as the three essential pillars for the younger generation."Technology and digital assets have no meaning if there is no island of commitment, compassion and character to harness them," he said, emphasising that India had immense technological capabilities as well as the trust and faith of its patients.Mangaluru woman attacked with iron rod in car; man arrested for attempted murder Highlighting the importance of patient-centred healthcare, he said the biggest asset of the country was not technology but the faith patients placed in healthcare professionals. He urged medical graduates to remain grateful to patients and dedicate their knowledge and skills to reduce human suffering.Referring to Swami Vivekananda's historic address at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, Prof Lal said the spiritual leader's teachings on character and social responsibility remained relevant even today. He called upon graduates to give back to society in whatever way possible and make service an integral part of their professional lives.He also cautioned students against becoming overconfident about their digital knowledge in the age of artificial intelligence. While acknowledging AI as an extraordinary technological advancement, he stressed the need to ensure that technology was used responsibly and did not become a threat to humanity.Drawing a parallel with the destructive consequences of nuclear technology, he said humanity must ensure that artificial intelligence was not misused. He urged students to follow the ideals of Swami Vivekananda rather than blindly placing their faith in technology.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, he said the country could achieve the goal even earlier if the younger generation developed an enlightened mindset and worked with a sense of responsibility.Referring to India's rich medical heritage, he recalled the contributions of Sushruta, regarded as the father of surgery, and Charaka, regarded as the father of medicine. He said their prime focus was healing and relieving the suffering of patients.Nitte DU Chancellor N Vishal Hegde presided over the gathering. Degrees were conferred on 1455 graduates.&nbsp;

primary_source.headline: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
primary_source.content: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope notA long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up the Death Star. Peer into the cosmic tea leaves and it would become immediately clear that no amount of evildoing could withstand a neurotic gold butler, a dustbin with ideas above its station and a walking seven-foot tall shagpile carpet with a very low tolerance for disagreement.It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.” Continue reading...

primary_source.content: When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom• The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come trueIt is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills.These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. Every Call of Duty, Halo or Grand Theft Auto release would have fans queueing outside branches of Game or Electronics Boutique, many dressed as favourite characters. Continue reading...

primary_source.content: The star is excellent in her return as a midlife assassin. But her whiny son is so annoying, the drama disintegrates into a soggy spy sitcom – he might just have killed the whole showSo there’s an assassin, right? Except, it’s not just AN assassin, it’s THE assassin. The world’s top assassin. Going round doing the most elite assassinations you can think of, being paid millions to kill super-dangerous people. Right? OK, But … it’s a woman – no, not like in Killing Eve. Well, OK, it is quite a lot like Killing Eve but wait: it’s not just a woman, it’s a sarcastic middle-aged British woman who hasn’t got time for anyone’s shit, And she’s got a difficult relationship with her adult son who doesn’t know she’s a killer! stories.primary_headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada

primary_source.headline: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American’s view of Canada
primary_source.content: The veteran travel writer turns his eye for detail on his northern neighbour and its peoplePaul Theroux’s arrival in Canada doesn’t go well. An immigration officer called Sweeney finds a small pocketknife in his car and fines him $500 for failing to declare a weapon. “I’m going to make you famous,” he angrily tells her, stumping up. Maybe he will, with this book. Canadians are reputed to be polite and easygoing, “slaves to their courtesy”, but the country has changed enormously in recent years. Will Theroux find it stuffed with Sweeney-ites? Luckily the answer is no.He issues a warning that, after 11 previous travel books, this may be his last; global overtourism appals him and so does much travel writing. But he shares Jack Kerouac’s delight in being on the road, and from his home in Massachusetts it’s just a four-hour drive to the border. His purpose is less to check out “the strangers next door” than to visit the village of Yamaska, in Quebec. It was there that a Frenchman called Antoine Theroux settled in the 17th century; a dozen or more Theroux families still live there; one local street is called Rue Theroux. The author isn’t only made welcome but presented with a certificate of honour by the local mayor. He repays the honour with a long chapter of family history. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: ‘It’s a new world. It’s a little fascistic. And it needs a different response’: U2 on 50 years together – and why Bono can’t work with Trump
primary_source.content: After some so-so albums, can U2’s new one, Carnaval de Luz, restore them to glory? They discuss male egos, working with Dolly Parton, and explain why, despite Trump, they still believe in democracy – at least in their bandLa Petite Maison, in Nice, has a certain reputation as a five-star celebrity haunt. Beyoncé eats here. So do Elton John, Tom Cruise, Harry Styles and Leonardo DiCaprio, their meals presided over by the restaurant’s founder, Nicole, variously described in print as “eccentric”, “unique” and “truculent” (she’s standing by the entrance when I arrive, and suffice to say, doesn’t look like someone you’d much enjoy being on the wrong side of).It’s enough of a celebrity haunt that the arrival of U2 – still incontrovertibly one of the biggest bands in the world 40 years after they could first reasonably have called themselves such – causes barely a murmur of interest among their fellow lunchtime diners. Then again, Bono is a regular. He was eating on the outdoor terrace the night of Nice’s terrorist attack, on Bastille Day in 2016, in which 86 people were killed. “I climbed through that window and hid under there,” he nods, pointing to a table at the rear of the restaurant. “Nicole,” he adds, “didn’t hide.” Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Minister sets Dec 31 deadline to complete railway overbridges
primary_source.content: Tiptur: Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti V Somanna has directed officials to expedite the construction of railway overbridges at various locations in the town and make them ready for inauguration by December 31.He was speaking after inspecting the ongoing construction of railway overbridges near the railway stationm Sharadanagar on Hassan Road and Honnavalli.Karnataka 'sting operation': H D Kumaraswamy is being intentionally targeted, says MoS SomannaExpressing displeasure over the slow pace of work, Somanna said, “During my previous visit, I had instructed officials to complete the works within the stipulated deadline. However, progress has not been as expected.”“While you are able to execute works swiftly in Hubballi and Bengaluru, why there is a delay here? Arrange adequate manpower and machinery and speed up the work. If the projects are not completed within the deadline, notices will be issued to the contractors and they will be blacklisted,” the minister warned.Residents also brought to his notice the poor condition of the temporary road provided for vehicular movement alongside the construction sites. The road is riddled with potholes and becomes muddy during rain, causing inconvenience to commuters.Stressing that the public should not be put to hardship, Somanna directed officials to repair the road immediately and send him photographs of the work through WhatsApp.He said the survey for Bengaluru-Tumakuru four-line railway project has been completed and the detailed project report (DPR) is ready. The project, estimated to cost around Rs 5,000 crore, has been sent for approval by the Union Cabinet, he added.Somanna urges Amit Shah to include Kadugolla community in ST listA unit of the Container Corporation of India has come to Tumakuru, while a Greenfield Corridor project is also being planned, “With Bengaluru expanding rapidly, the necessary infrastructure must also be extended to Tumakuru. primary_source.headline: Wipro appoints Angan Guha as President and CEO for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: Wipro Limited on Friday announced the appointment of Angan Guha as President and Chief Executive Officer for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit, effective December 8, 2026. He will report to the CEO and Managing Director, Srini Pallia, and serve on the Wipro Executive Leadership Team.In this role, Guha will focus on strengthening the business and market momentum across BFSI, Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing, and accelerating growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients in the region.Wipro headcount falls by 6,716 in Q2, biggest decline in recent quarters“We are delighted to welcome Angan to Wipro’s leadership team,” said Srini Pallia, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Wipro Limited. “His experience in driving business growth, combined with his focus on innovation and execution, will be valuable as we strengthen our Americas business. I am confident that his leadership will help us accelerate growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients," he added.“The evolving AI landscape presents unprecedented opportunities for businesses to innovate and lead. I look forward to collaborating with the talented team at Wipro and helping clients navigate this transformation, drive meaningful business outcomes, and build on Wipro’s strong consulting and technology capabilities,"&nbsp;Angan Guha said.Guha is an experienced technology and business leader who has spent more than three decades driving growth, digital transformation and client success across BFSI, Energy & Utilities and Manufacturing, Wipro said. Prior to serving as Global CEO & Managing Director of Birlasoft Ltd., Guha spent over 28 years at Wipro, holding several senior leadership roles, including CEO of the Americas 2 Business Unit and member of Wipro’s Leadership Team.

stories.primary_headline: Commercial crop cultivation not a right under FRA; tiger habitat non-negotiable: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Commercial crop cultivation not a right under FRA; tiger habitat non-negotiable: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: In a stern message against attempts to legitimise commercial farming inside protected forests, the Supreme Court on Friday held that cultivation of a commercial crop cannot be recognised as a forest right under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, and cannot justify occupation or continued presence in forest areas. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta declared that the sanctity of critical tiger habitat must take absolute precedence. “We must remain conscious of the fact that with Megamalai reserve forest being declared as a Tiger Sanctuary/reserve, the sanctity of the critical tiger habitat has to be given primacy over any claim which intends to encroach upon the forest area,” the court observed.Supreme Court clarifies OBC creamy layer ruling will not reopen past appointments, selections or promotionsThe Tamil Nadu government urged the court to allow silk cotton cultivation in the Megamalai region on historical grounds. To the State’s reliance on historical cultivation of silk cotton, the bench ruled, “cannot, by itself, establish that such cultivation constitutes a forest right” under the FRA. Section 3(1)(c) of the Act recognises only the right to ownership, access, collection, use and disposal of minor forest produce traditionally gathered within or outside village boundaries. Silk cotton is not traditionally collected as minor forest produce, the bench said.The court noted the State's affidavits instead revealed “the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop.” “The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crop is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” the court said. “Planned or promoted cultivation of a commercial crop inside the forest areas is completely impermissible as no such right is recognised under FRA, 2006,” it added.Consequently, the bench said the claim that silk cotton cultivation itself justifies the presence of cultivators was “wholly unacceptable.” Tamil Nadu’s Revenue Department had claimed 2,767 persons residing outside forest boundaries were cultivating the crop. The court, however, said outsiders cannot cultivate inside forests without external financing or facilitation. It directed the court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to examine this aspect thoroughly for action against violators. The CEC has also been asked to give its opinion on whether silk cotton qualifies as minor forest produce. Building on its May 29, 2026 judgment that ordered structured, time-bound eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the Agasthyamalai landscape—including division-wise eviction plans, removal of encroachments and a ban on new non-forestry activities—the bench issued further hard directives. Claims of Forest Dwelling Scheduled Tribes or Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must be decided strictly under Section 6 of the FRA and its Rules, not on present occupation alone, it said.Persons in Categories II and III identified by the State are excluded from FRA consideration. The State has been given a final 30-day window to form remaining Gram Sabhas, the bench ordered.The court set up a Special Committee headed by former Chief Justice of India B R Gavai, assisted by a CEC officer and Tamil Nadu’s Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, to scrutinise FRA orders and report to the court in a sealed cover.The matter will be listed on February 1, 2027 for an interim status report. The CEC has also been directed to respond to an NHAI application concerning the NH-744 Puliara–Edamon tunnel proposal.

stories.primary_headline: 1,800 dubious books, inflated prices: Periyar library row triggers DMK-TVK blame game

primary_source.headline: 1,800 dubious books, inflated prices: Periyar library row triggers DMK-TVK blame game
primary_source.content: Chennai: No one in Tamil literary circles has ever heard of Agalvilakku Pathipagam. But the hitherto unknown publication house has supplied about 1,800 books to the Periyar Arivulagam, a modern library built at a cost of Rs 300 crore in Coimbatore, inaugurated by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay in October.The procurement of never-heard-of books from a dubious publication house has raised questions of a mega scam in buying books for the library, a pet project of former Chief Minister M K Stalin. The alleged scam came to light after acclaimed Tamil author Perumal Murugan, whose brilliant works have been translated into English and other languages, visited the library in Coimbatore and found these books on the racks on the fourth floor."Whatever the case may be, it is certain that a massive scam has taken place in the procurement of books. New publishing houses have been started solely to supply books to this library. Books have been generated using artificial intelligence with outdated technology,” he alleged in an article on Sindhai, a Tamil magazine.&nbsp;‘Exorbitant prices’The contents of the books supplied by the publication house in question are mostly generated using artificial intelligence (AI), containing false information and distorted facts about the history of Tamil Nadu, and were procured at exorbitant rates.For instance, a 300-page book titled Naladiyar: Vaazhvin Vazhikaati is priced at Rs 1,445. To top it all, Agalvilakku Pathipagam functions from an apartment in Madipakkam, a locality in Chennai, and its owner refused to speak to the media.Moreover, some of the authors whose books have been procured have never been heard of, and their names sound fake, such as Trisha Vijay, Thamarai Karthi, Madhu Sakthi, Malathi Sethuraman, and Keerthi Govind. Other interesting names of authors of books published by Agalvilakku Pathipagam that still adorn the library racks are Vijay Balu, Vijay Selvam, Vijay Adithan, and Sumega Vijay.Data quoted by the Information Integrity Desk (IID) — the TN Government’s fact-check unit — shows that all 2,393 books published by the publications with names of authors were registered between December 3, 2024, and February 6, 2026. A total of 609 author names, including the name Trisha Vijay, were also registered.Murugan, who was also part of the committee with over 100 members to recommend books for the library, demanded that the books be removed from the shelves immediately to ensure books with distorted facts don’t find space.Tamil Nadu CM slams DMK, says author Perumal Murugan exposed graft in buying books during its regime How did this happen?While the committee with over 100 members from various genres of the literary field was constituted in November 2025 under the then DMK government to suggest books to be purchased for the library, documents seen by DH show the books were delivered to the library between March 2026 and June 2026 — during the transition period, including the Assembly elections and after TVK assumed office.Questions remain on how these dubious books were bought by the library without checking, and when the School Education Department issued the order for the said publication. Except for Agalvilakku Pathipagam, other books in the library are of good standards.As expected, the allegations of a scam set off a blame game between the DMK and TVK. Interestingly, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay took to his X page as TVK chief to deride the DMK as the “most corrupt party,” which didn’t even spare a library in the name of Periyar.&nbsp;The DMK hit back at the CM for blaming the party and demanded an impartial investigation — it alleged that only books procured from the said publication and another were received at the library in June 2026. Other opposition parties also strongly condemned inclusion of dubious books in a world-class library. &nbsp;‘Members were asked recommendations’DH spoke to a couple of members of the committee who said the orders for procurement of books were issued online and members were asked for recommendations only on the subjects they were experts in.&nbsp;“We were asked about the books to be bought in a particular stream and we gave our recommendations. We were not aware of who got the orders. Not all members were consulted on all subjects. Every stream had a set of experts and professors,” a member said.Another member said some of the procured books, which he was informed about, were of “good standard” and will help library visitors.Conceived by the previous DMK government, the construction of the swanky library spread over an area of about 2 lakh square feet was almost complete when the TVK assumed office in May 2026—the former Chief Minister said recently his predecessor just cut the ribbons.Murugan’s sarcasmMurugan said he had never heard of Agalvilakku Pathipagam in his 40 years of experience as a writer. “It appears that my world of reading and search for knowledge has become so narrow,” he wrote sarcastically.Naladiyar: Vaazhvin Vazhikaati is another book that caught Murugan’s attention, not just for its exorbitant price of Rs 1,445 for 350 pages but also for its false content. The book describes Naladiyar — a classical Tamil Jain poetic work — as one of the important poets and philosophers in Tamil.&nbsp;“I have been teaching Tamil for three decades, but I never learned that Naladiyar was a philosopher,” he added.Turning the tables on the DMK, the IID said a GO was issued on November 5, 2025 constituting a committee to procure books worth Rs 50 crore for the library and on January 9, 2026, the committee selected books for procurement following which negotiations were held on January 24.&nbsp;“Based on this, approval was obtained at a high-level committee meeting held on 05.02.2026 to place orders for the selected books.&nbsp;Subsequently, on 06.02.2026, the coordinating committee for special libraries recommended a list of books and issued a purchase order for their procurement. Accordingly, 60,266 books worth Rs 19.19 crore were procured for the Periyar Knowledge Centre,” the IID said.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Deepinder Goyal’s brain chip stirs backlash from medical doctors, they call it ‘clinically bankrupt’

primary_source.headline: Deepinder Goyal’s brain chip stirs backlash from medical doctors, they call it ‘clinically bankrupt’
primary_source.content:
Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has again found himself at odds with the medical fraternity over his brain monitoring device ‘Temple’ which will be soon available for pre-order in the country in a variety of six shades, Goyal had informed.While his pre-order post has gained a lot of attraction among people, many medical doctors are contesting against it, with the internet famous the LiverDoc calling it ‘fraudulent’.Goyal has allegedly positioned the Rs 85,000 wearable as a ‘fitness’ and ‘well being’ tracker and refrained from calling it a medical product.Designed to rest near the temple, the device has promised to measure entropy, a body metric indicating how hard the body may be working to meet its energy demands.It also alleges to measure ‘cerebral blood flow’ using light-based optical sensors that sit against the skin.&nbsp;Though the company backs the efficacy of the product with an internal experiment on 23 adults and 44 young men, compares its progress to other smart fitness devices that are released before the conclusive results are presented before the public, the medical community stays sceptical of the move, saying its reliability remains unsubstantiated.Dear Concerned Indian Doctors,I see your rage against Temple on X. I have a few points to make:1. First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren't true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple. We have 14-day,…&mdash; Deepinder Goyal (@deepigoyal) November 5, 2026
 

Temple, smart wearable will be up for pre-order this weekend: Deepinder GoyalGoyal versus doctorsIn a heartfelt note on X, Goyal said that he stepped down as CEO of Eternal, parent company of Zomato and since then devotionally worked towards building this fitness product.He said that his company has spent nearly 30 million dollars on its development, out of which 20 million dollars have come from his own pocket.He also informed that the product also carries a 14 days return policy and the customers are willing to give it a try.However, at this juncture, many medical doctors interrupted the flow of his messages and said no amount of emotional struggle, future promises and financial support can substantiate the efficacy of a fitness or health product.They also called out lack of clinical evidence as the biggest drawback with the product.According to some clinicians, including the LiverDoc, the fitness tracker can only measure scalp level blood flow and is not a suitable metric to assess any neurological disturbance.As per reports, light-based sensing systems can only have a superficial depth up to 1 or 2 cm. This may translate only to the outer cortex of the brain.&nbsp;The science used to run this product may not be as effective as a deep tissue ultrasound or a perfusion MRI which can assess blood flow velocity across various regions of the brain.In his defence, Goyal reassured that for now Temple is primarily a fitness product.When DH asked medical doctors on the utility of the fitness tracker, they said it may not have any clinical purpose and the readings obtained might be purely relative.However, some people on X have supported Goyal while saying that no innovation is perfect and lack of absolute evidence must not stop researchers from exploring the potential.To the people disparaging the Indian medical community, please note that we, me included, are not against technological solutions towards improved preventative care. In fact, preventative care is is the heart of medical science.But, let us not confuse fradulently selling… pic.twitter.com/5riczT3cli&mdash; TheLiverDoc™ (@theliverdoc) November 6, 2026
 

Comparing it to other fitness toolsWhen medical professionals questioned Goyal as to why there are no peer reviewed studies on his product, he said that many fitness trackers get released to the public before a comprehensive report of their efficacy is made available to all.“Most wearable companies start with internal studies. Whoop shipped its band in 2015, and the first published validation followed a few years later. We hold ourselves to a higher standard; pre-prints are a step prior to peer reviewed publications, and they are coming up,” said Goyal on X.However, his post attracted a rebuttal where critics like LiverDoc and other clinicians argued that Apple and Fitbit passed multisite clinical trials for FDA clearance.“Other wearables like Whoop (which he cited) measured and validated exactly what the wearable can measure within limits of human anatomy and physiology,” said LiverDoc.Some came in support of Goyal, saying “Indians punish entrepreneurs for taking risks.”However, medical doctors stood their ground by saying they are not against innovation but clinical evidence is the backbone of any fitness or clinical invention.Ending his response on X, Goyal said that some of the features of Temple are not even made public and some of them have nothing to do with doctors.As the line gets blurred between a fitness tracker and medical technology, Temple may have to cover a long path to gain support of healthcare workers.

brief_bullets: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal faces intense backlash from the medical community over his new wearable device, 'Temple,' which claims to monitor cerebral blood flow and entropy. Despite Goyal investing $30 million into the project and positioning it as a fitness tool rather than a medical product, prominent clinicians, including the LiverDoc, have labeled the device 'clinically bankrupt' and fraudulent. Critics argue that the light-based sensors lack the depth required for accurate neurological assessment, rendering the data scientifically unsubstantiated. While Goyal defends the product’s efficacy and offers a 14-day return policy, medical experts maintain that emotional narratives and financial commitment cannot replace rigorous clinical validation, highlighting a growing tension between tech-driven wellness innovation and established medical standards.
why_it_matters_bullets: The controversy underscores the risks of unregulated health-tech products bypassing clinical validation to influence consumer wellness decisions.

primary_source.headline: ‘It’s in our blood’: Lebanon, Ukraine and Syria rugby league teams fly the flag despite horrors of war at home
primary_source.content: Players from war-torn countries say they are determined to ‘give people hope’, ‘put the country on the map’ and ‘wear the badge with honour’By No Helmets RequiredThere are many reasons for a country to not play rugby league. Being at war does not seem to be one of them. Last Sunday, a few miles apart in Sydney, Syria and Lebanon played international fixtures on contrasting stages. Syria hosted a series of friendlies at the humble home of Bankstown Bulls, before Lebanon played an all-time World Cup classic against France in a frenzied CommBank Stadium. A few days earlier, Ukraine had played a crucial European Championship match in Belgrade.Lebanon beat France after a wild finish, suggesting they are still among the top eight teams in the world, even if their ranking is far lower due to their inactivity since the last World Cup. The country has been torn apart by the war in the Middle East. “Our last game together was in England in 2022,” said prop Jalal Bazzaz, who played in all three of Lebanon’s matches at the World Cup. “So our aim was just to be good each week. We talked about giving back to where we come from, our roots. It’s in our blood. To put on that jersey, represent my country and put Lebanon on the world stage – it gives people something to smile about, a bit of hope. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme

primary_source.headline: India, EU conclude multi-billion Euro global innovation programme
primary_source.content: New Delhi: India and the European Union have concluded negotiations on New Delhi's association with a Euro 93.5 billion flagship research and innovation programme, paving the way for expanded collaboration under their broader strategic partnership.The decision comes weeks before India and the 27-nation bloc are set to seal a landmark free trade agreement -- billed as the "mother of all deals" -- to create a market of two billion people.The European Commission and India have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi's association to Horizon Europe programme, the EU said.American midterm results will not have an impact on India-US interim  trade deal: SourcesThis marks an important step forward for EU-India relations, strengthening scientific cooperation, creating new opportunities in research, and deepening the strategic partnership, it said.India's association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years.For researchers, businesses and research organisations across Europe, India's association will open up more opportunities to collaborate with Indian partners and build lasting scientific and technological links, the EU said.Once the agreement is signed and the necessary procedures are completed on both sides, researchers and organisations in India will be able to receive funding directly from Horizon Europe and lead collaborative projects under its Pillar II: 'Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness', it said.This is the largest part of the programme which funds collaborative, multi-national research and innovation projects tackling societal and technological issues, such as health, digital, industry, space, climate, energy, and bioeconomy.The EU said the move will create new opportunities for European and Indian partners to pool expertise, develop technologies and address shared challenges.Association is the closest form of cooperation offered by the EU to non-EU countries under Horizon Europe.It allows organisations in associated countries to participate on equal terms with their EU counterparts in the parts of the programme covered by the agreement. In return, associated countries contribute financially to the programme.The successful conclusion of negotiations clears the way for the signature of the association agreement, subject to the completion of the necessary procedures on both sides. The two sides are likely to sign the formal agreement in January.India and the EU had launched the exploratory discussions on the Horizon programme in February 2026 and formal negotiations began in July.EU-India scientific cooperation builds on the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation, signed in 2001 and renewed until 2030.Research and innovation also form an integral part of the Joint EU-India Comprehensive Strategic Agenda towards 2030, adopted at the summit talks between the two sides in New Delhi on January 27.The partnership has been strengthened through the EU-India Trade and Technology Council, which facilitates collaboration on key digital areas such as artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, semiconductors, high-performance computing, digital skills and the sixth generation of wireless telecommunications.The EU and India took a further step in collaboration on digital skills through the launch of the first-ever European Legal Gateway Office in India last February, aiming to facilitate safe, legal and well-informed mobility to the EU in the ICT sector.Horizon Europe runs from 2021 to 2027, with a budget of Euro 93.5 billion.International cooperation is central to the programme, bringing together expertise and resources to advance scientific excellence and innovation.Currently, 23 non-EU countries are associated with Horizon Europe. They are: Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Canada, Egypt, the Faroe Islands, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Korea, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Switzerland, TÃ¼rkiye, Tunisia, Ukraine and the United Kingdom.The India and EU ties have witnessed a major upswing in the last few years.The two sides are set to sign the free trade deal next month.

stories.primary_headline: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess

primary_source.headline: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
primary_source.content: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporateOver a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat. Mike Myers kicked off this unexpected tradition by embodying the furry, anarchic Dr Seuss character for a notoriously, almost defiantly ghastly 2003 live-action treatment. After doing us all the service of killing flesh-and-blood Seuss movies for good, Myers was later followed by a more charming Martin Short (via voiceover on a cute PBS/CBC animated series) and now Bill Hader, stepping into the role for a big-budget animated reboot from the oft-flailing animation division of Warner Bros.Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. stories.primary_headline: NHAI issues guidelines for barrier-less Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling on national highways

primary_source.headline: NHAI issues guidelines for barrier-less Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling on national highways
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has released new guidelines to standardise the design and infrastructure of toll plazas on four-lane and wider national highways, paving the way for wider adoption of the barrier-less Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system across the country.The guidelines ensure that upcoming and ongoing national highway projects support free-flow toll collection, allowing vehicles to pass without stopping at booths. This is expected to eliminate queues, cut waiting times and fuel consumption, and make journeys safer and more seamless.Explained | Barrier-less toll plaza in Delhi; how does it work?The policy circular sets uniform standards for plaza layouts, lane configurations, gantries, road infrastructure, lighting, signage and supporting facilities, the NHAI said in a statement. With vehicles tolled electronically without physical barriers, the number of lanes required has been rationalised compared with conventional plazas, enabling more efficient use of space and smoother traffic flow.These norms will apply to all future and under-construction projects. Projects at the Detailed Project Report stage must incorporate the new designs, while those already awarded or under construction will adopt them through contractual provisions. NHAI field offices have been directed to implement the requirements in upcoming works and facilitate changes in ongoing ones, the statement  from NHAI said.The guidelines emphasise adequate lighting, advance guidance through signage and Electronic Variable Message Signs, and the construction of an administrative building-cum-operations and maintenance centre. These measures aim to improve visibility, keep users informed and support efficient plaza management.The move builds on earlier NHAI guidelines for high-speed access-controlled national highways and marks a significant step toward a uniform barrier-less tolling framework nationwide.

stories.primary_headline: Childminder who left more than 20 children alone in her home jailed

primary_source.headline: Childminder who left more than 20 children alone in her home jailed
primary_source.content: Childminder who left more than 20 children alone at home jailed More than 20 unattended children, two under the age of one, were in Amanda Mathewson's house in Dunfermline, Fife, when she was arrested in August 2024. Her offending only came to light after concerned parents spied on her leaving for a school run without their children. An internal Care Inspectorate probe found Mathewson, who was been licensed to look after eight children under the age of 16 at any one time, had been tipped off about inspections by an unknown staff member. Sheriff John MacRitchie said Mathewson had committed a "gross abuse of a position of trust" during sentencing at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court. He read victim impact statements from parents of affected children who described them suffering from "nightmares and anxiety" and developing a "distrust of childcare providers".

stories.primary_headline: 'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up

primary_source.headline: 'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up
primary_source.content: Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago The 21-year-old's career path has been very similar to that of his 23-year-old brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players. Both were stars of the Birmingham City academy before big-money moves to the German Bundesliga and England call-ups. Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days - 69 days older than Jude when he made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side. The central midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to £31m. Jude also moved to Dortmund when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid. Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling.

stories.primary_headline: Yaxel Lendeborg is the NBA’s most entertaining rookie – and he’s not holding back

primary_source.headline: Yaxel Lendeborg is the NBA’s most entertaining rookie – and he’s not holding back
primary_source.content: The Warriors’ freshman has spent his first weeks in the NBA antagonizing superstars, speaking his mind and emerging as one of the league’s most compelling personalitiesIf a screen-addled pickup basketball player teleported into the body of a high-level athlete, they might resemble Yaxel Lendeborg. The most commonly cited fact about Lendeborg is that he used to spend 12 to 14 hours a day gaming, and didn’t debut on his high school basketball team until he was an upperclassman. Professional athletes often have origin stories that resemble the superhero more than the mortal, but Lendeborg really was just like us at one point. Lendeborg has also said that prior to entering the NBA, he didn’t really watch it, either. The Puerto Rican forward racked up more than enough accolades in college to qualify for the NBA, including helming Michigan to their first national championship in 37 years, but still. Any of you reading this could smoke the man who may be this season’s rookie of the year in trivia about his profession.The 24-year-old Lendeborg is a forward on the Golden State Warriors, a team caught between the ancient, gleaming remnants of the most fearsome dynasty of the 2010s and its future. The balance didn’t work out last season, as the Warriors produced flashes of old greatness to win one play-in game before flaming out in the next. Such results are a frustrating waste of Stephen Curry’s wonderful form even at 38 years old. Lendeborg is the best hope in a while to help maximize it. But even more importantly, Lendeborg is the character of the season so far. He’s spent its first two weeks antagonizing superstars, firing off unselfconscious takes in the press and vacuuming up the spotlight from his blander peers. What a joy to bear witness to an athlete who probably didn’t even hear the words “media training” until college. Continue reading...
