brief_bullets: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has rapidly emerged as the NBA’s most compelling personality, blending an unconventional background as a former competitive gamer with elite on-court production. After leading Michigan to a historic national title, the 24-year-old forward has transitioned seamlessly into the professional ranks, where his unfiltered demeanor and willingness to antagonize established superstars have captivated the league. As the Warriors navigate the twilight of their championship dynasty, Lendeborg’s arrival provides both a necessary infusion of youthful energy and a potential catalyst to maximize Stephen Curry’s remaining prime. His authentic, media-untrained approach stands in stark contrast to his peers, establishing him as an early frontrunner for Rookie of the Year and a vital cultural force.
why_it_matters_bullets: Lendeborg’s emergence provides the Warriors with a critical bridge between their aging dynasty and a viable, high-impact future.

Welcome to Edition 9.18 of the Rocket Report! Blue Origin packed a lot of news into one afternoon Thursday with the reveal of a new kick stage for the New Glenn rocket, a new rocket engine design, and the minor and widely expected delay for New Glenn's return-to-flight mission from December until January. The reconstruction of Blue Origin's wrecked launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida, continues apace after a catastrophic explosion nearly six months ago. There's a lot of pent-up demand from NASA, Amazon, and the Space Force for Blue Origin to get New Glenn back in action.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). SpaceX vets work on water-fed propulsion. Three brothers who worked at SpaceX in the Falcon 9 era are now building satellites that run on water, a potentially harvestable resource on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, Ars reports. In late 2022, the three Carlisle brothers founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. Argo Space's satellites will use water not only as a propellant, but also as a coolant and radiation shield.Read full article

primary_source.content: Zugspitze is Germany's highest mountain with an altitude of 2,962m (9,718 ft) The teenager called emergency services and was eventually rescued on the mountain at an altitude of about 2,500m (8,200ft). brief_bullets: A recent YouGov survey across six European nations reveals that while a vast majority of citizens acknowledge human-driven climate change and support urgent intervention, public enthusiasm wanes when policies demand significant personal lifestyle sacrifices. stories.primary_headline: Rocky review – 50 years on, Stallone’s boxer remains an exhilaratingly gritty contender

primary_source.headline: Rocky review – 50 years on, Stallone’s boxer remains an exhilaratingly gritty contender
primary_source.content: The actor’s triumphant breakthrough has clear ancestors in grimy tales of working-class struggle, but finds a fresh, rousing idealismPeter Farrelly’s new film I Play Rocky is about the underdog-with-heart story of how a great boxing movie got made against the odds with its plucky young untried screenwriter allowed to star. So here is a reissue of that 1976 film for its 50th anniversary. It’s a forthright, rousingly idealistic film, wholesome in its essential patriotism, and which unselfconsciously shrugs off the boxing-movie’s gloomy generic inheritance, throwing away its grim traditional baggage of tragedy, cynicism and loss. It also doubles as a love letter to Philadelphia, the cradle of American democracy.Its writer and insurgent star Sylvester Stallone created the role of Rocky Balboa, a punchy heavyweight fighter just turned 30, making peanuts slugging it out with bums and reduced to collecting debts for the Philly mob; this is an indignity which infuriates his grizzled old trainer and former mentor Mickey (Burgess Meredith) who once saw greatness in Rocky and is disgusted to see him selling out. Rocky is moreover entirely oblivious to national preparations to celebrate the 1976 bicentennial. (Boxing is for this anniversary what country music was in Robert Altman’s Nashville, only without the disorientation and pessimism.) Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Jerusalem artichokes are nutty and delicious, but will run rampant if you let them
primary_source.content: Once this tasty tuber is established in your garden, you’ll have a crop for life. Great news – if you can digest themIt’s intriguingly rare to see a crop of jerusalem artichokes, considering how easy they are to grow. They’re part of the sunflower family and, surprisingly, entirely unrelated to the globe artichoke. They produce tall, leggy stems upon which a bright yellow flower blooms, and while they lack the size and sturdiness of sunflowers, they make up for that by appearing in great numbers and developing edible tubers underground. Despite these admirable features, there are good reasons why they are not the most common sight.First, though nutty and delicious, these tubers can be quite hard to digest – earning them the nickname “fartichokes”. They contain a carbohydrate that can be tough on the gut, so it’s recommended that they are cooked well and introduced into your diet incrementally. Having said that, some eat jerusalem artichokes raw, so to those who are devoted to them, or have a fierce digestive system, they’re never off the menu. The second reason they’re not that common, I suspect, is that once you’ve planted them, you’ve probably got them for ever – and, wow, do they know how to run rampant. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Nikita Gill: ‘I read Flowers in the Attic too young. Someone should have stopped me’
primary_source.content:
The Indian-Irish poet on the Mahabharata retelling that inspired her to write, Arundhati Roy’s courage, and the poetry of Lucille CliftonMy earliest reading memory
  My father was a sailor and my mother a teacher. They were both voracious readers. I was lucky enough to come from a home full of books and when we joined my father out at sea for extended periods of time, my mother carried plenty of books for me to read. I remember sitting by the porthole in our cabin, looking out at the sea on a sunny day, the ship moving calmly through the waters. I was reading The Tale of Peter Rabbit by Beatrix Potter, a book that still feels like a dream. I was four years old.My favourite book growing up

primary_source.headline: Enrico Rava Fearless Five with Joe Lovano: Corners review | John Fordham's jazz album of the month
primary_source.content: (ECM)The Italian trumpeter’s group – featuring an old friend – rip through originals and free improvisation while balancing late-Miles funk with excellent vocals and horn balladsMiles Davis was the gamechanger behind at least three landmark transformations in jazz-making methods between the late 1940s and the 1960s – yet he was perhaps too instinctively lyrical, and too worldly, to take the freedoms he helped unleash too far from the marketplace. In 1960s Europe, a different story emerged, as African American free jazz innovations by Ornette Coleman, John Coltrane, Albert Ayler and others flowed into cultural traditions from Scandinavia to Spain, Soviet Russia and East Germany, inviting unions with contemporary classical and local folk music along the way.But Miles’s unique sound remained as a key inspiration to two gifted trumpeters in Poland’s Tomasz Stańko (1942-2018) and the Italian Enrico Rava, even as they also drew on European eclecticism. Rava continues to rip through the walls of linear post-bop mazes, and use raw sound as if it were his everyday speech, just as Miles once did – as confirmed by Corners, recorded with his young Fearless Five group plus his longtime friend Joe Lovano on saxophones. stories.primary_headline: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices

primary_source.headline: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
primary_source.content:
Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password.
The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.
One connection, works every time, needs no retries
There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts.Read full article

primary_source.headline: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
primary_source.content:
NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years.
The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4.
“The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” Isaacman said. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.”Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable

primary_source.headline: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
primary_source.content:
Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools. Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn't want to use AI. Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing.
The gist of the new policy, according to Google's blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts.
When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times, which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it's probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google's educational AI system will operate. Google's approach may not be entirely altruistic, but it technically offers schools more choice and control than they have now. Instead of Google turning off search, it will let schools make that decision based on their internal AI policies.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets

primary_source.headline: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
primary_source.content:
With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet.
While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets.
Point spreads
Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: The Guardian view on the midterms and foreign policy: American voters spoke, and now the world waits anxiously | Editorial

primary_source.headline: The Guardian view on the midterms and foreign policy: American voters spoke, and now the world waits anxiously | Editorial
primary_source.content: The Democrats have gained new powers to constrain Donald Trump. But the drubbing that Republicans received could yet prompt him to new excessesDonald Trump is a president without parallel, but history can still be instructive. Lame duck presidents often focus on foreign policy to escape domestic discontent and establish a legacy in an area where a hostile Congress offers less of an obstacle. Mr Trump, who was stunningly rebuffed by voters in Tuesday’s midterms, might seek satisfaction in construction projects, the 2028 presidential race and his family’s future. Or, amid the humiliation and with Republican critics growing louder, he could distract attention with fresh adventurism – perhaps escalating against Cuba – or more likely a vengeful new offensive against Iran.Mr Trump won’t put in the legwork or attention to detail demanded by, say, Bill Clinton’s push for lasting peace in the Middle East. But he loves the glitz of state visits, spectacular military action, hobnobbing with strongmen and (unearned) credit for dubious “peace deals”. With a potential three-way meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping mooted for the Apec summit in China this month, Ukraine, Taiwan and others have reason to be nervous.Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? stories.primary_headline: MAHA lost bigly in the midterms—is it at death's door?

primary_source.headline: MAHA lost bigly in the midterms—is it at death's door?
primary_source.content:
As Democrats blew away their Republican rivals in an unprecedented midterm sweep Tuesday, the Make America Health Again movement also got bowled over, raising questions about the fate of the motley movement.
MAHA—which has centered around anti-vaccine activist and current Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.—saw many of its favored candidates and allies lose, while vocal adversaries of Kennedy won. And the coalition was splintering under stress even before the voting started; in recent months, supporters have accused Kennedy and the Trump administration of inaction and betrayals in their two years in power.
Now hobbled in Washington, shedding supporters, and showing little to no influence in voting booths, is MAHA on its deathbed? Or will it be reborn—possibly into a new group? Could it be assimilated into a blue platform—after sloughing off the more repulsive, conspiratorial aspects of Kennedy's ideology? These are the questions circling in the aftermath of Tuesday's bloodbath.Read full article

primary_source.headline: ‘Disco’ movie review: Stylish treatment fails to paper over the lack of substance in this generic mafia story
primary_source.content: Just like Ullas Chemban’s debut work Anchakkallakokkan, Disco too is strong in its technical department, but that is not enough to save a film which banks a little too much on stylistics

sources.headline: ‘Disco’ movie review: Stylish treatment fails to paper over the lack of substance in this generic mafia story

brief_bullets: Director Ullas Chemban’s latest feature, Disco, has drawn critical scrutiny for prioritizing aesthetic flair over narrative depth. While the film showcases impressive technical proficiency, echoing the stylistic choices seen in Chemban’s debut, Anchakkallakokkan, reviewers argue that these visual flourishes fail to compensate for a derivative and hollow mafia-themed screenplay. By relying heavily on superficial genre tropes rather than substantive storytelling, the production struggles to distinguish itself within a saturated market. Ultimately, the film serves as a cautionary example of how high-end cinematography and polished production values cannot salvage a project lacking a compelling, original foundation, leaving audiences with a visually engaging but emotionally detached experience that fails to resonate beyond its surface-level presentation.
why_it_matters_bullets: The film highlights a growing industry trend where technical polish often masks fundamental weaknesses in narrative development and originality.

stories.primary_headline: Factories commence cane crushing

primary_source.headline: Factories commence cane crushing
primary_source.content:
Belagavi: Sugar factories in Belagavi district are all set to commence the 2026-27 sugarcane crushing season, albeit over a month behind schedule.Of the 29 functional sugar factories in the district, 12 are privately owned and 17 are co-operative units. While the factories rely on mechanised harvesting, they also bring in harvesting gangs from Maharashtra to cut the sugarcane.Over the past week, several factories symbolically lit their furnaces to mark the commencement of the crushing season. However, actual crushing and harvesting activities remained stalled as farmers continued their protests demanding higher prices for sugarcane.Karnataka sugarcane farmers withdraw protest, accept Rs 3,600 per tonne price and profit-sharing deal with factories The protests, spearheaded by the Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha and Hasiru Sene, had continued for over a month, with farmers demanding prices that adequately cover cultivation costs and provide a reasonable profit, besides a share in the profits from the sale of sugar and its by-products.The deadlock was broken after sugar factories agreed to pay Rs 3,600 per tonne and share profits based on increases in sugar prices, following which farmers decided to withdraw their agitation.During the previous crushing season too, farmers had staged protests at Gurlapur in Mudalgi and succeeded in securing an increase in sugarcane prices.Sugarcane price row: Farmers to stage ‘Jail Bharo’ on November 2This season, their demands included a price of Rs 5,500 per tonne, comprising Rs 4,500 from sugar factories and a government support price of Rs 1,000 per tonne, funded through taxes generated from the sale of sugar and its by-products. They also demanded that the Centre increase the minimum selling price of sugar from the existing Rs 31 per kg to Rs 60 per kg, arguing that this would help address the recurring issue of inadequate sugarcane prices.The agitation prompted Union Food and Consumer Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi to constitute a committee to examine the farmers’ demands, including an increase in the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane, a revision of the minimum selling price of sugar and other demands raised by the protesters.Farmers had blocked traffic on the busy Pune-Bengaluru National Highway at toll plazas in Kognoli in Nippani taluk, Hattargi in Hukkeri taluk and Hirebagewadi in Belagavi taluk. They had also organised a march to lay siege to Joshi’s residence in Hubballi. The march was called off after Joshi assured them that their demands would be considered by November 26.Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had met the protesting farmers at Channamma Kittur and subsequently held discussions with them at Suvarna Vidhana Soudha and the Circuit House in Belagavi. However, these interventions failed to break the deadlock. November 2, farmers launched a jail-bharo agitation, offering to court arrest in support of their demands.Farmers intensify agitation 
in sugarcane-growing districts of north KarnatakaThe breakthrough came after District In-charge Minister Satish Jarkiholi held discussions with representatives of farmers and sugar factories on November 3 and 4. Following the meetings, the factories agreed to pay Rs 3,600 per tonne and also accepted a profit-sharing formula linked to increases in sugar prices.Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha and Hasiru Sene state president Chunappa Pujeri said the organisations had decided to withdraw the agitation following the agreement on higher sugarcane prices and profit-sharing.“Farmers could get up to Rs 4,350 per tonne this season, and we are hopeful of securing this amount, given the shortage of sugarcane across the world. Sugar factories will now commence crushing operations, and harvesting will begin,” he said.

primary_source.headline: Brand's barrister refers himself to regulator after report he confronted journalist
primary_source.content: Ian Winter, left in this court sketch, reportedly verbally clashed with a reporter who had previously investigated his client In a Times and Sunday Times podcast on Thursday, Rosamund Urwin said she introduced herself to Ian Winter KC outside court after verdicts were delivered. She claimed he responded with a "snarl" and said "I hope you're pleased with yourself". "Apparently I said, but I can't actually remember this but I've read it in reporting, 'I am pleased that justice has been done'", Urwin said. She said that Winter replied "it wasn't" and suggested she was to blame using a profanity. In a statement, Winter said the "ways matters have been characterised" in the media  meant they should be "subject to proper scrutiny".

stories.primary_headline: Centralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru

primary_source.headline: Centralised street light monitoring system promises better public lighting in Bengaluru
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda, on Friday, inaugurated the city's first Centralised Control and Monitoring System (CCMS) for streetlights. The centre established in Jayanagar is aimed to improve the condition of streetlights and automate the operations significantly.&nbsp;According to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), across the city, close to five lakh LED streetlights, comprising three lakh newly installed LED lights and 1.97 lakh existing LED lights will be integrated with CCMS and 24677. The initiative will also help bring down expenditure on power since it is expected to provide over 54% energy savings.Dark streets, delayed smart lighting: Bengaluru’s LED upgrade struggles to get on trackThe system, once implemented across the city, will help improve the public lighting infrastructure across the city significantly since it has a capability to flag problems automatically. “The key advantages of this technology is its ability to proactively detect faulty or non-functional streetlights. This will enable maintenance teams to identify and attend to faults without waiting for citizens to report them. The advanced CCMS will enable centralised as well as individual monitoring of streetlights, automated ON/OFF scheduling, GPS-based asset tracking, real-time energy consumption monitoring and automatic identification of non-glowing, flickering and partially glowing streetlights,” a statement by the GBA said.Better streetlights and faster turn around time for repair will also improve public safety, Gowda said. “Beyond energy savings and reduced electricity expenditure, the initiative is expected to improve road illumination, enhance public safety, reduce maintenance response time and minimise energy wastage,” he said.GBA chief inspects Bengaluru West infrastructure projects, directs fast-tracking of worksIn the coming days, GBA plans to have four dedicated Streetlight Central Control Rooms across the city. These control rooms will monitor streetlight performance, electricity consumption and fault alerts through a centralised digital dashboard.The GBA is also planning to set strict timelines for the repair of streetlights identified to be faulty.&nbsp; “Dedicated field maintenance teams will be deployed to address identified faults and citizen complaints, with a provision to resolve streetlight-related issues within 24–48 hours of identification or registration. Failure to resolve faults within prescribed time limits will automatically trigger penalties on maintenance contractors,” the statement by GBA said.Streetlights are one of the highest reported problems in the city apartment from waste management. DH had earlier reported that close to 6,000 complaints were reported regarding faulty streetlights in September and on average close 5,000 complaints are being reported every month.

stories.primary_headline: ‘He left the world in ruins’: the author who defied the Taliban and burning tyres to tell Alexander the Great’s epic story

primary_source.headline: ‘He left the world in ruins’: the author who defied the Taliban and burning tyres to tell Alexander the Great’s epic story
primary_source.content: He is the most powerful ruler ever – and his first biographer was crucified. What drew Edmund Richardson, winner of the £50,000 Baillie Gifford prize, to his short tumultuous life?He was the most powerful man in the world but he was brought down by one battle too many after a decade at the top. The story of Alexander the Great might be more than 2,000 years old, but it seems timely that a new biography of the ancient ruler won the Baillie Gifford prize for nonfiction just as President Trump took a battering in the US midterms. “This is a moment,” says its author Edmund Richardson, “where people are finding that there are limits to what unlimited wealth and power can do, and that humanity catches up with you, whether you like it or not. Alexander wants to transform the world – and he leaves it in ruins.”Wearing a purple velvet jacket, purple scarf and matching socks, with a high forehead and corona of auburn curls, Richardson himself might have stepped out of an earlier age. It is hard to imagine anyone less like history’s favourite mob boss than this softly spoken professor of classics. We are having coffee at the offices of the PR company for the Baillie Gifford prize, the view of the City of London skyline from the floor to ceiling windows a reminder of 21st-century power and economics. stories.primary_headline: Government contingency plan ready for drop in rabi sowing

primary_source.headline: Government contingency plan ready for drop in rabi sowing
primary_source.content: New Delhi: It is too early to raise alarms over a sharp drop in rabi sowing this season, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Friday, stressing that adequate time remains for planting and that the government has prepared a contingency plan for the first time.As of October 30, total rabi acreage stood at 37.56 lakh hectares, down 46 per cent from 69.02 lakh hectares a year earlier, according to official data.Wheat, the main winter crop, covered just 19,000 hectares against 3.34 lakh hectares last year. Pulses fell to 9.45 lakh hectares from 19.56 lakh, oilseeds to 20.97 lakh from 38.62 lakh, and other crops also lagged.“Sowing can be undertaken till December. The current month is crucial,” the official said, attributing the delay largely to a 13 per cent deficient monsoon that left residual soil moisture low in many areas.The ministry has drawn up a dynamic contingency plan covering 225 districts to address moisture stress and weather variability. Farmers in water-scarce regions are being encouraged to grow less water-intensive crops such as chickpea, mustard, lentil and millets. Climate-resilient and heat-tolerant seeds are being promoted.Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has directed officials to accelerate sowing after the kharif harvest and make optimal use of remaining moisture. The government reports adequate stocks of fertilisers and certified seeds, with supply chains coordinated down to the district level.A soil health policy aimed at cutting chemical fertiliser use is expected in the next three to four months. Officials also noted a sharp decline in stubble-burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana, stating it is not a major contributor to Delhi-NCR pollution, while efforts continue to reduce edible oil import dependence.

stories.primary_headline: Telangana woman studying in US goes missing after stepping out for evening walk

primary_source.headline: Telangana woman studying in US goes missing after stepping out for evening walk
primary_source.content: Hyderabad: Talking to their daughter, who studies in the US, every day was a routine for Koya Yadagiri Reddy and Roopa of Shabdulapuram village in Nalgonda district, Telangana. They spoke to her before she left for college and again after she returned from her part-time job. Since November 2, however, there has been no word from Sreeja Koya, 23, who has gone missing in Boston, USA.Sreeja, their only daughter, was last seen after she went out for an evening walk. “On November 2, after she came back from work, her roommates were to celebrate the birthday of one of them. As is her habit, she went out for an evening walk, promising to be back for the celebration. But she did not return, and her roommates tried to reach her. At first, the phone rang, but she did not pick up. After some time, it was switched off. They then contacted us in India to asked if she had called us. We were clueless and worried about what happened to her,” a distressed Yadagiri Reddy said on Friday.Local reports in the US said Sreeja lives in the Dorchester area of Boston and was last seen at around 9.45 pm local time at Edison Green, wearing a black jacket and blue jeans. She is suspected to be near Carson Beach or Harbor Point. Her friends filed a complaint with the Boston Police on November 3, and on November 4, the Boston Police Department issued a missing person alert.Sreeja KoyaPolice are learnt to be focusing on several areas based on the last known location of her mobile phone and are searching in particular around Carson Beach and Harbor Point.According to family members, Sreeja was determined from childhood to pursue higher education in the US. She left for the US last year and is studying at the University of Massachusetts in Boston. Alongside her studies, she works part-time at a recently secured job on the university campus. The family has also appealed to Telugu associations and the Indian diaspora in the US to help trace her.“Koya was last seen leaving her residence in the area of Edison Green in Dorchester at approximately 9:45 PM on Monday, November 2, 2026. Koya is described as an Indian female, 5’3”-5’5” in height, with a thin build and black hair. Koya was last seen wearing a black jacket and blue jeans. She may be in the area of Carson Beach or Harbor Point. The Boston Police Department is actively working to locate Sreeja Koya and urges anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to call 911 or contact District C-11 (Dorchester) Detectives at (617) 343-4335. Community members wishing to provide information anonymously may do so via the CrimeStoppers Tip Line,” said the Boston Police Department in a missing person alert.

primary_source.content: Moderna lifts annual revenue forecast on strong COVID vaccine demand overseas  Reuters

sources.headline: Moderna lifts annual revenue forecast on strong COVID vaccine demand overseas - Reuters

brief_bullets: Moderna has raised its full-year revenue forecast, citing robust international demand for its updated Spikevax COVID-19 vaccine. The biotechnology firm now anticipates annual revenue between $3 billion and $3.5 billion, surpassing previous conservative estimates as global health authorities accelerate autumn vaccination campaigns. CEO Stéphane Bancel attributed this positive momentum to strong commercial execution and successful regulatory approvals across key overseas markets, which have offset declining domestic interest. By securing significant procurement contracts and streamlining its supply chain, Moderna is effectively stabilizing its financial outlook despite the broader post-pandemic market contraction. This strategic pivot underscores the company's ability to maintain a sustainable commercial footprint while transitioning its mRNA platform toward a diversified portfolio of respiratory and personalized cancer therapeutics.
why_it_matters_bullets: The upward revision signals a resilient commercial model for mRNA technology, bolstering investor confidence in Moderna’s long-term financial viability.

stories.primary_headline: Show HN: Agentic Identity Broker, OAuth Delegation for AI Agents

primary_source.headline: Show HN: Agentic Identity Broker, OAuth Delegation for AI Agents
primary_source.content:
Hi HN, I’m Jan. I am co-author of the Agentic Identity Broker (AIB), an MIT-licensed OAuth2 broker in the Zalando Incubator, that lets a user give an AI agent scoped, revocable access to MCP services.The broker solves three major challenges that are especially relevant in corporate environments: (A) Enable users to delegate workloads to agents without providing the agents all the user’s tokens. (B) Connect fragmented identity and authorization systems. (C) Centralize tool approvals and audit logging.We built AIB to fill an infrastructure gap in our own agent platform. At this moment in time, IETF working groups are still finalizing standards for agent identity, and vendors are still turning the necessary infrastructure into off-the-shelf products. We needed that infrastructure today.How it works: the user consents once per agent and service. The broker stores the third-party tokens encrypted. At request time a gateway (e.g. Agentgateway) does RFC 8693 token exchange. Agents never see user tokens and MCP servers only implement tools and don’t need to care about all the OAuth 2.1 plumbing.AIB is v0.1 and runs in production, bringing together hundreds of our agents with dozens of internal and external MCP servers.To try it locally: clone the repo, run "just compose-up-detached".The current features focus on on-behalf-of (OBO) use cases, where human actors delegate to agents. Next we are looking to also support headless agents, where agents are invoked by machines. Intent-based authorization is yet another package on our roadmap. If you’ve built either, or have feedback on the UI/UX, I’d like to hear from you!

Points: 11

stories.primary_headline: Centre orders rice stock disclosure, clears southern states to curb hoarding

primary_source.headline: Centre orders rice stock disclosure, clears southern states to curb hoarding
primary_source.content: New Delhi: With rice prices rising amid a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers nationwide to declare their rice and paddy stocks. It also permitted five southern states to impose stock limits to check hoarding.Under a November 6 order, all such entities must declare holdings in six categories—Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy—on the Food Stock Portal every Friday. Unregistered units or those breaching limits face action under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.Separately, the Centre consented to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana imposing stock limits on paddy and rice until January 31, 2027. Authorities will monitor compliance to ensure availability and prevent black marketing.Karnataka teacher conserves 1,540 traditional rice varieties, earns national recognitionTo boost supplies, additional rice has been allocated to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, with a focus on southern states. The Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) e-auction target for 2026-27 has been doubled to 50 lakh tonnes from 25 lakh tonnes. About 25 lakh tonnes were sold by October 31, more than double last year’s figure for the same period.Trade experts link the price rise to uneven rainfall, which has driven inflation especially in premium non-Basmati varieties. Retail rice inflation climbed to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with average prices around Rs 48.23 per kg—about 12% higher than a year ago.Kharif paddy acreage fell nearly 4% to 42.68 million hectares. Output is estimated at 147 million tonnes against last year’s record 154 million tonnes. While government stocks remain comfortable, pressure is sharper in southern premium grades such as Sona Masoori.

primary_source.content: (Virgin)The reunion that fans were hoping for turns out to be a cash-grab box set – though there is a worthwhile curio featuring Posh on lead vocalsIs there a more taunted fanbase than that of the Spice Girls? Seemingly every other week a story – usually perpetuated by Mel B, the band’s number one cheerleader – appears in the tabloids hinting at some sort of reunion. Or film. Or documentary. Swift denials then emerge, typically linked to Geri or Victoria, and all is calm until a week or so later.So when teasers showing landmarks from 1996’s Wannabe video suddenly appeared on the band’s official social media accounts in September, it felt as if the fans had something tangible to celebrate. The comments quickly filled with hopes of another reunion tour following 2007’s full-band jaunt and 2019’s Posh-less stadium trek. In a music landscape littered with nostalgia tours, surely Ginger, Scary, Baby, Sporty and (maybe) Posh could strap on some Buffalo boots for a final zig-a-zig-ah? Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Another day, another U-turn: Congress on Election Commission directive on those left out of draft rolls

primary_source.headline: Another day, another U-turn: Congress on Election Commission directive on those left out of draft rolls
primary_source.content: New Delhi: With the Election Commission deciding to provide another opportunity to electors left out of draft voter lists in seven states where SIR is ongoing, the Congress on Friday termed it a "U-turn" and said this is a "belated admission that wrongful deletion and exclusion" has taken place.The opposition party also reiterated its demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar must go and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls must be suspended.Facing allegations of disenfranchising crores of voters, the Election Commission on Friday gave a fresh chance to electors of seven states who were marked as Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate (ASDD), and whose names could not be included in the draft rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.In a letter, the EC directed the chief electoral officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland to facilitate the inclusion of such electors in the final electoral rolls.SIR | Election Commission gives deleted electors one more chance to submit enumeration forms Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said, "Another day, yet another U-turn. The Election Commission of India has just issued instructions to include left-out voters in the on-going SIR in seven states/UTs.""This is a belated admission that wrongful deletion and exclusion has indeed taken place under the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate) category," Ramesh said on X.The ECI is carrying out corrective-after-corrective following the nationwide outrage and anger over SIR which has robbed over 13 crore Indians of their constitutional right to vote, he said."Every new set of orders begs the question: what was the point of this bureaucratic mess that every Indian has been put through? These repeated clarifications and amendments actually expose the true intent of the diabolical PM-HM (Narendra Modi-Amit Shah). They have been caught out," Ramesh said."SIR is the latest form of Vote Chori. And now that the Chori has been caught, the ECI and the PM-HM duo are doing everything to cover their tracks," he alleged.Every corrective also reinforces what has become abundantly clear -- Gyanesh Kumar must go and SIR must be suspended, Ramesh added.The EC has also asked officials to establish a monitoring mechanism to ensure that no eligible elector is deprived of the opportunity to be included in the Final Electoral Roll, while preventing duplicate enrolments.The EC's decision covers electors who were issued enumeration forms but whose forms were not received back, resulting in their exclusion from the draft rolls.The opposition has accused the EC of deleting the names of crores of eligible citizens from the electoral rolls at the behest of the BJP. The poll authority has defended the revision, citing its validation by the Supreme Court.

stories.primary_headline: Fake call centres in India targeted elderly US citizens; stole $27.39 million

primary_source.headline: Fake call centres in India targeted elderly US citizens; stole $27.39 million
primary_source.content: Hyderabad: The investigation by Enforcement Directorate sleuths in Hyderabad over fake call centres that targeted US nationals has identified 927 approved collections totalling about $27.39 million (around Rs 261 crore) between July 2025 and September 2026. The proceeds were collected in the US and routed through accounts of companies in the UAE (Dubai) and Hong Kong, and through crypto-assets, before reaching India through hawala and angadia channels.They were then converted into Indian rupees through cryptocurrency and hawala networks. The syndicate ran organised calling floors in which staff worked as dialers, bankers and closers. Kerala man loses Rs 7.7 lakh in online scam using S.I.R. as pretextUS nationals were first contacted on the pretext of fraudulent purchases or charges on their accounts. Callers posing as officials of US agencies then intimidated them, using forged identity cards, badges, official letters and court documents.Under threat of legal action, victims were induced to hand over cash and gold to pick-up persons, send cash in parcels through courier services, transfer funds to the US bank accounts of money mules, or purchase gift cards.Earlier, ED had conducted search operations on September 15 under Section 17 of the PMLA at four premises in Patiala, Pune and Chandigarh, wherein three live call centres, two at Patiala and one at Pune, were detected with around 220 persons working at the time of the searches.The operation spanned several countries. Calls were placed from India to residents of the United States using lead lists of about 20 lakh persons, US telephone numbers and auto dialler servers hosted in Germany and Finland.Andhra CID cracks transnational crypto investment fraud, arrests 8One of the main accused, Harshil Nayanbhai Raval, who was arrested by ED on Wednesday, maintained the master accounts of the operation at fake call centres, recording the profits out of the earning of fake call centres, partners’ shares and remittances of Proceeds of Crime (PoC) to Dubai, and invested the proceeds in properties.Another accused Jaswant Singh coordinated cash pick-ups from victims in the US through pick-up teams and parcels, routing the cash to the network for conversion into Indian Rupees through tokens and hawala. Chetan Munjal, a 25% partner of M/s Rabditta Corporates, which runs the Kala Ghoda restaurants which received proceeds of crime of Rs. 23.19 lakh, provided the protection to the call centre and received the funds out of PoC for the said call centres.“The WhatsApp groups of the calling floors record 927 'approved' collections of about US$ 27.39 million (about Rs. 261 crore) between July 2025 and September 2026, received from victims as gold, cash pick-ups, cash parcels sent through courier, wire transfers, Bitcoin and gift cards. The seized devices further record 397 US bank accounts held in at least 15 US banks, including Wells Fargo (313 accounts), SSB Bank, Bank of America, Thread Bank, Column N.A. and Lead Bank, into which victims were made to wire or deposit money. These accounts were held by recruited money mules, by victims whose accounts had been taken over, or in stolen or synthetic identities; in four cases the online banking log-in details of the victims were also found,” said ED sources.Crypto-assets were a major channel for moving the proceeds. Collections were converted into USDT (Tether) on the TRON network and into Bitcoin, and victims were also made to deposit cash at Bitcoin ATMs. The consolidated analysis of the digital evidence seized during the search has so far identified 549 US nationals as victims and targets of the syndicate, whose names and particulars were found recorded on the seized devices. Besides, 6,463 US telephone numbers were called or messaged from the seized phones.

stories.primary_headline: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop

primary_source.headline: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop
primary_source.content:
Elon’s Edsel is no more. Last night, Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed on social media that his car company is ending its failed attempt to wrest control of the American pickup truck market. The Cybertruck will cease production in the middle of 2027, liberating that space in Tesla’s cavernous factory for other uses—more Cybercabs, most likely.
Musk first revealed the Cybertruck in late 2019, back when Tesla was still trading at a theoretically understandable price-to-earning ratio. The pickup's unusual angular shape owed more to low-res video game models than any concessions to practicality. At the time, Musk made fanciful claims that the truck would use a stainless steel monocoque construction, telling his audience that “the body and bed don’t do anything useful” on a normal truck. While some race cars use carbon-fiber monocoques for strength and lightness, making a pickup truck with a stainless steel monocoque chassis would only make sense if someone had an awful lot of stainless steel lying around and needed something to do with it all.
The truck was supposed to go on sale for less than $40,000, and Tesla made its usual stratospheric sales predictions that (had they been accurate) the bare metal EVs would be as ubiquitous as the Model 3 and Y.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: ‘I’m never going to be bloody Robert De Niro!’: Rob Brydon, the most chipper man on TV

primary_source.headline: ‘I’m never going to be bloody Robert De Niro!’: Rob Brydon, the most chipper man on TV
primary_source.content: The nicest man in acting is back with new comedy, Bill’s Included. He talks about rejecting Hollywood, refusing to play a villain – and why he just can’t make fun of Steve Coogan‘I’m a nice person, you know,” says Rob Brydon, as I met him in a basement green room of the BBC, where probably nobody with such a mellow ego has ever sat. “I am a people-pleaser. That’s who I am.” It’s an unnecessary clarification – at 61, he’s been nice on TV, as himself and in character, for most of our adult lives.We’re here to talk about his new six-parter, Bill’s Included, but his character in it, the eponymous Bill, is such a distillation of pure Rob Brydon that it’s (accidentally, he says) a celebration of his entire career. As the show opens, Bill has just been left by his wife, who’s run off with the gardener. At no point does he ever fire the guy – “I like him!” – but otherwise, his life is completely upended. The utterly plausible cocktail of his civic mindedness and howling loneliness drives him to take in four lodgers, local university students. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: After the midterms, the global right is reeling. But the danger of Trumpism will never be gone | Jonathan Freedland

primary_source.headline: After the midterms, the global right is reeling. But the danger of Trumpism will never be gone | Jonathan Freedland
primary_source.content: Yes, the Republicans suffered humiliating defeat. But the fact that a Trump presidency was even possible means something like it could happen againHe’s down, but not quite out. Barring divine or other intervention, Donald Trump will remain in the Oval Office for a further two years and 10 weeks. Or, as the White House put it in a plaintive social media post brimming with neediness: “PSA [Public Service Announcement]: Trump is still your president.” But that’s not the only reason why the global celebrations that greeted the Democratic tidal wave that swept Republicans out of even their deepest heartlands should be tempered, if only a tad.Don’t get me wrong, the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections are cause for genuine international jubilation. The defeats of Trump allies in Serbia and Brazil were delicious appetisers, but this was the feast. No mere electoral setback in line with midterm tradition, this was a thorough repudiation of the second Trump presidency and of Trumpism. The 16% swing to Democrats in the popular vote for the House of Representatives was greater even than the 11.2% swing recorded in the Watergate midterms of November 1974, following the resignation in disgrace of Richard Nixon. Trump had worked hard for many months to undermine these elections, either by gerrymandering districts in his favour or preparing the ground for a later claim the vote was rigged, but to no avail: the democratic system proved too resilient, and the American public too determined to have their say. And have it they did, in a voice loud and clear. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together

primary_source.headline: Hockey’s streaming spree means there’s one fewer thing holding Canada together
primary_source.content: A shared joy of the sport has united Canada for much of its history. But it’s becoming increasingly difficult – and expensive – to watch games on televisionThe Oilers lost to the Detroit Red Wings on 26 October, but Edmonton captain Connor McDavid got an assist anyway. He’s been doing that a lot lately. Just 16 games into the year, McDavid has 31 assists. It’s the fastest anyone has ever hit that milestone in any NHL season. But on that night in late October, many fans in Edmonton were unable to see McDavid’s feats – including patrons of a local bar – because it was one of nine Oilers games this season that are only available via a subscription to a premium streaming service.It’s the same story in every Canadian NHL city, thanks to changes to broadcasts that have meant that a handful of games for each team are now only available with a C$12.99 per month subscription to Sportsnet+, a streaming channel owned by Canadian telecom juggernaut – and owner of the Toronto Maple Leafs – Rogers Communications Inc. But it’s not just Sportsnet+. The NHL also expanded its broadcast deal with Amazon, so when, two nights after the game against Detroit, the Oilers played their provincial rival, the Calgary Flames, only Amazon Prime subscribers could watch (true to form, McDavid got two assists in that one). Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom

primary_source.headline: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom
primary_source.content: She started acting at six and by 16 was starring in Even Stevens with Shia LaBeouf. Then her career fell apart. Here, she explains how she survived growing up in the spotlightIn a class at college, Christy Carlson Romano was encouraged to think about her “community”. Who were their people, the tutor asked the class, and where did they belong? The answer that popped into Carlson Romano’s head was child actors, but not the ones that went on to have successful grown-up careers. “The ones who were once the shining stars,” she writes in her memoir, “and who are now just trying to find out their places in the world.” Carlson Romano had returned to college after initially dropping out. She had survived sexual assault and toxic relationships, was broke and drinking too much. But before all that, she had been a teenage Disney star. She had made it.The title of her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck, gives you a flavour of where Carlson Romano, 42, is coming from, but what’s most striking isn’t that she goes off the rails (she doesn’t, hugely, compared to other former child stars), but how sensible and mature she is as a child. It’s alarming. When fans recognise her now – she was in the popular Disney series Even Stevens which started in 2000 – they tell her she was a huge part of their childhoods. She had been acting the part of a normal suburban girl, the perfectionist Ren Stevens, while having no idea what that was like. She was already a mini adult. Continue reading...

primary_source.content: The Romanian auteur’s new film could have been the kind of homogenous ‘Europudding’ he’s railed against for years. Instead, it’s a culture-clash skewering of conservative and liberal values worthy of its Palme d’Or‘Pffff!” Cristian Mungiu lets out an exasperated sigh. We are sitting in the basement of a London hotel, at the end of a long morning of back-to-back interviews for the Romanian film-maker, and his press handler has just snuck into the room to remind him of his next appointment across town. But Mungiu blanks him and leans on to his table, because he wants to tell one more story.In 2013, Mungiu was part of a delegation of European auteurs who travelled to Brussels to meet the then president of the European Commission, José Manuel Barroso. At the time, the EU and US were in talks to slash barriers to trade between the two economic blocs, and the film-makers were lobbying the Commission to spare their industry from the deal. Clothes discarded in the US, Canada and Europe arrive in the city to be torn back into fibres and spun into yarn, feeding a textile recycling industry that supplies markets across the world.Suraj, 19, had travelled from West Bengal state to work in Panipat’s factories, following his cousins and friends who had already found jobs there. He hoped to earn enough to send money home to his parents. But in late August, an electrical short circuit in the machine propelled him into the shredding mechanism. The accident crushed both arms. stories.primary_headline: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

primary_source.headline: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments
primary_source.content: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee". She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too. The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary. Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates. Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs. They repay 9% of anything they earn over £25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off. The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.

stories.primary_headline: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook review – the heir to a legendary eatery … who sets soup on fire

primary_source.headline: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook review – the heir to a legendary eatery … who sets soup on fire
primary_source.content: She is completely baffled in the kitchen, but the star valiantly resurrects her family’s famous restaurant. Her journey is chaotic, hilarious – and deeply movingIt starts both very well and very badly does Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook. On the one hand, our host’s absolute ignorance of how food works – or pans, or knives, or plates – has a refreshing authenticity about it. Too often in these shows, in which a celebrity goes on A Journey to acquire basic knowledge in what is generally considered to be a normal field of human endeavour, their lack of exposure to it or inability therein is pretended or hammed up. But actor, rapper and comedian Awkwafina – real name Nora Lum, which is what she uses for this series beyond the title, for reasons that will become clear – is the real, wholly baffled deal.Non-game recognises non-game, and as a kitchenphobe myself, I see the truth in her crouched stance by the oven or hob, fearful yet hostile to anything they may ask of her. We see her pour milk over a couple of eggs she has just lobbed doubtfully into a pan, the tentativeness with which she approaches spatulas and ladles, the hatred in her eyes when presented with raw ingredients – it all speaks to someone who has remained truly untouched by the culinary arts and was, at least until a commissioning editor approached with an idea, happy to remain so. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković

primary_source.headline: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković
primary_source.content: The Student List has shown my generation, who protested against the Milošević regime in the 1990s, how we should have done itOn Halloween, a few days after a student-led movement swept aside an illiberal, seemingly invincible regime in my native Serbia, I was sitting on the Vienna tram and watched various friendly and malicious monsters getting on and off around me. Witches, devils and unicorns were politely making their way to their respective parties.Not all monsters wear fancy dress. Later that evening, I walked past a Serbian restaurant; in front of it stood a group of grumpy-looking men. They were smoking, spitting and swearing. I recognised the hardened, couldn’t-care-less attitude, the smell of corruption, the penchant for violence. Yet they looked as though their lives were coming to an end. These men are the losers of the revolution that is taking place in Serbia. Their smuggling routes and deals are under threat. Their criminal networks no longer function. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Sony revives the original Walkman headphones, adds USB-C

primary_source.headline: Sony revives the original Walkman headphones, adds USB-C
primary_source.content:
Color us nostalgic.
Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player.

      In this marketing image Sony shared, you can see the Walkman TPS-L2.
        Credit:
          Sony
      
Originally called the "MDR-3L2," the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. primary_source.content: The masterful Australian writer has become a kind of prophet – and his dramatic and moving new essay collection challenges us not to look awayTim Winton has been working his themes for almost 50 years in a palimpsest of 32 books: family, manhood, land and ocean; what it is to be human and Australian; intimate pleasures and anxieties that feed his fiction. The distinctive quality of his new collection of memoir and essays, Songs from the Firefront, is urgency verging on panic. He’s an elder in his 60s, with limited time to get his messages across before we all go up in flames.Living on the western edge of Australia, Winton has been an eloquent climate-change activist for decades. He has fought, with tenuous success, to protect Ningaloo Reef. He entrances us with Scheherazade stories that blend crystalline nature writing and terrifying facts. stories.primary_headline: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven

primary_source.headline: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
primary_source.content:
BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 2027 i7 as well as the 2027 iX5 and X5. Ars does not accept paid editorial content.
When BMW debuted the new 7 Series in 2022, it set a new standard for large luxury sedans, increasingly irrelevant though that class is. Rather than siloing off an electric alternative like Mercedes, with its EQS alongside the normal S-Class, BMW simply made the powertrain an option. Stick with a V8 if you want, or consider the rather good electric version instead—only subtle differences like the badging and lack of exhaust pipes give the game away.
Since then, BMW has brought out a string of even newer electric vehicles for the 5 and 3 Series (plus their SUV counterparts). It has switched from battery packs made of prismatic cells to more energy-dense arrangements of cylindrical cells. The motors are still electrically excited synchronous ones, but now the drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging.
This sixth-generation electric powertrain was designed for the clean-sheet Neue Klasse family, which also threw out the legacy cruft of dozens and dozens of discrete single-function electronic control units for a handful of powerful domain controllers. These computers take over those functions but with much faster processing power—and therefore more capabilities in terms of chassis control or powertrain efficiency—as well as the ability to be more easily updated.Read full article

Kalshi is having a bad week in the federal court system. Two circuit appeals courts rejected the prediction market's latest attempts to block state gambling laws in Connecticut, New York, and Nevada. Kalshi is separately facing a new lawsuit filed by the Arkansas attorney general.
In all cases involving Kalshi and state governments around the US, the main issue is whether state gambling laws apply to prediction markets despite Kalshi's claim that its platform offers "swaps" that can only be regulated by the US Commodity Futures Exchange (CFTC). The Trump administration is on Kalshi's side, with Donald Trump Jr. serving as an advisor to Kalshi in exchange for a generous equity deal.
"Kalshi insists that its products are not gambling," but "Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin said yesterday when announcing his lawsuit against Kalshi. Kalshi's prediction market lets customers "wager money on the outcome of just about anything" despite the fact that "gambling on an unregulated platform is squarely prohibited by Arkansas law," he said.Read full article
